difficultyReason: Straightforward observational stimulus with one clear quantitative fact and a simple hedged inference. The correct answer uses modest language ('some') that directly follows from the data.
stimulus: A pharmaceutical company conducted a clinical trial of a new antibiotic on 500 patients with bacterial infections. After treatment, 480 patients showed full recovery within two weeks.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The antibiotic is guaranteed to cure all bacterial infections.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some patients treated with the antibiotic recovered fully within two weeks.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All patients with bacterial infections will eventually recover if given this antibiotic.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The antibiotic is more effective than older antibiotics.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who do not recover from bacterial infections should never use this antibiotic.

explanations.correct: 480 out of 500 patients recovered, so it is certain that some patients recovered. This is a modest, hedged claim fully supported by the data.
explanations.A: Too strong — 20 patients did not recover, so the antibiotic is not guaranteed to work.
explanations.B: Correct — the data directly supports that at least some patients recovered.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus says 480 recovered within two weeks; it does not address eventual recovery for all.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus provides no comparison to other antibiotics.
explanations.E: Unsupported and inverted — the fact that some patients did not recover does not mean those patients should never use it.

difficultyReason: Three related facts establishing a clear correlation. The correct answer draws a modest conclusion about the relationship between the facts.
stimulus: A study of workplace productivity tracked employees over six months. Workers who took regular breaks reported higher job satisfaction. These workers also completed their assigned tasks on time more often than workers who took few breaks.
questionStem: The information above most strongly supports which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Regular breaks eliminate workplace fatigue.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All workers must take regular breaks to meet deadlines.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some workers who take regular breaks complete their tasks on time more often than some workers who do not.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Taking breaks is the only way to improve job satisfaction.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Employees who avoid breaks are less competent.

explanations.correct: The study found that break-takers completed tasks on time more often. The hedged phrasing 'some workers who take breaks' vs 'some workers who do not' directly follows from this comparative data.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus does not say breaks eliminate fatigue, only that break-takers have higher satisfaction and better on-time completion.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus shows a correlation for this group, not that all workers must take breaks.
explanations.C: Correct — the data directly supports this modest comparative claim.
explanations.D: Too strong — breaks correlate with satisfaction, but the stimulus doesn't establish they are the only way.
explanations.E: Too strong and unsupported — lower on-time completion doesn't imply lower competence.

difficultyReason: Simple observational fact about plant behavior. Correct answer uses modest hedged language ('at least some') that is directly entailed by the stimulus.
stimulus: Researchers observed that plants in a greenhouse wilted when watered with salt water, but remained healthy when watered with fresh water. This pattern held true across 15 different plant species.
questionStem: Which one of the following inferences is most supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Salt water is toxic to all plants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: At least some plants wilt when exposed to salt water.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Plant species cannot survive in salt water under any circumstances.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fresh water is the ideal growing medium for all plant species.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Salt water causes permanent damage to plant roots.

explanations.correct: The observation that plants wilted with salt water across 15 species directly supports that at least some plants wilt under these conditions.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus shows wilting in these 15 species, not that salt water is universally toxic.
explanations.B: Correct — the data directly supports this hedged claim.
explanations.C: Too strong — wilting is not the same as inability to survive in any circumstance.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus only contrasts salt and fresh water in this greenhouse setting.
explanations.E: Too strong — the stimulus reports wilting, not permanent root damage.

difficultyReason: Economic data presented as simple fact. Correct answer is a modest inference about consumer behavior using hedged language.
stimulus: Sales data from a major retailer show that the average household income of customers who purchased luxury goods was significantly higher than the average household income of customers who purchased standard goods.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All people with high incomes purchase luxury goods.

choices.label: B
choices.text: People with low incomes never purchase luxury goods.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some customers with higher household incomes purchased luxury goods.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Income is the only factor that determines whether someone buys luxury goods.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Standard goods are inferior in quality to luxury goods.

explanations.correct: If the average income of luxury purchasers was significantly higher, then at least some customers with higher income purchased luxury goods. This is a direct, modest inference.
explanations.A: Too strong — not all high-income people need to purchase luxury goods.
explanations.B: Too strong — the data does not rule out any low-income luxury purchases.
explanations.C: Correct — the data directly supports this hedged claim about at least some customers.
explanations.D: Too strong — income correlates with purchase behavior, but is not established as the only factor.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus concerns purchasing patterns, not quality comparison.

difficultyReason: Environmental observation with clear temporal pattern. Correct answer uses hedged language about a trend that is directly supported.
stimulus: Over the past decade, the average annual rainfall in a particular region has decreased by 20 percent. Local farmers report that crop yields have fallen during this same period.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most support which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Decreased rainfall is the only cause of lower crop yields.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All farmers in the region have experienced losses in crop yields.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Rainfall changes affect agricultural productivity in at least some cases.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Crop yields will eventually return to previous levels.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Irrigation cannot offset the effects of reduced rainfall.

explanations.correct: The stimulus shows both a decrease in rainfall and a reported fall in crop yields over the same period. This supports a modest inference that rainfall affects yields in at least some cases.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus establishes a correlation but not exclusivity.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus reports that farmers report fallen yields, not all farmers.
explanations.C: Correct — the correlation between rainfall decline and yield decline supports this hedged claim.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus provides no information about future recovery.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus does not address irrigation or its effectiveness.

difficultyReason: Linguistic observation presenting a simple factual comparison. Correct answer uses modest language that directly follows from the data.
stimulus: A survey of 200 native English speakers found that speakers from the United Kingdom used the word 'whilst' in their everyday speech, while speakers from North America rarely used this word.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All English speakers from the United Kingdom prefer 'whilst' to 'while.'

choices.label: B
choices.text: North American English is inferior to British English.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some English speakers from the United Kingdom use 'whilst' in their everyday speech.

choices.label: D
choices.text: North American speakers are incapable of understanding 'whilst.'

choices.label: E
choices.text: 'Whilst' is becoming obsolete in all varieties of English.

explanations.correct: The survey found that UK speakers used 'whilst' in everyday speech, so at least some UK speakers use this word. This is a straightforward, modest inference.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus says UK speakers used the word, not that all prefer it.
explanations.B: Unsupported — linguistic differences do not establish superiority.
explanations.C: Correct — the data directly supports that at least some UK speakers use the word.
explanations.D: Unsupported — rarity of use doesn't imply inability to understand.
explanations.E: Too strong — the stimulus shows regional variation, not obsolescence across English.

difficultyReason: Historical fact with a clear stated outcome. Correct answer is a modest inference about the result using appropriately hedged language.
stimulus: In the 1970s, a law was enacted to restrict the use of certain pesticides known to harm the ozone layer. Following the enactment of this law, measurements of ozone concentrations in the upper atmosphere showed improvement over the next two decades.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The law was responsible for all environmental improvements during this period.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Pesticide restrictions are the only way to protect the ozone layer.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ozone concentrations improved at least in part due to the pesticide restrictions.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The ozone layer has been completely restored to its original condition.

choices.label: E
choices.text: All countries adopted similar pesticide restrictions in the 1970s.

explanations.correct: The stimulus presents a temporal sequence: law enacted, then measurements show improvement. A modest inference is that restrictions contributed at least in part to the improvement.
explanations.A: Too strong — the law's causal role in all improvements is not established.
explanations.B: Too strong — the stimulus doesn't establish exclusivity of method.
explanations.C: Correct — the temporal correlation and stated improvement support this hedged claim.
explanations.D: Too strong — improvement is not the same as complete restoration.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the stimulus concerns one law, not global adoption.

difficultyReason: Medical observation with a clear quantitative comparison. Correct answer is a modest inference using hedged language ('some') that directly follows.
stimulus: A study examined two groups of patients: those who took a vitamin supplement daily and those who did not. The supplement group reported fewer instances of common colds during the year-long study period.
questionStem: The information above most strongly supports which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Vitamin supplements prevent all common colds.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some people who take vitamin supplements experience fewer colds than some people who do not.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All people should take vitamin supplements to avoid colds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Colds are caused entirely by vitamin deficiency.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Vitamin supplements are more effective than medical treatments.

explanations.correct: The study found the supplement group reported fewer colds. This directly supports a modest comparison: some supplement-takers had fewer colds than some non-takers.
explanations.A: Too strong — fewer instances is not the same as prevention of all colds.
explanations.B: Correct — the data directly supports this hedged comparative claim.
explanations.C: Too strong — the stimulus shows a correlation for one group, not a universal recommendation.
explanations.D: Unsupported and backwards — the stimulus does not establish causation from deficiency.
explanations.E: Unsupported — no comparison to medical treatments is provided.

difficultyReason: Ethical scenario presenting two related facts. Correct answer is a modest inference about what the facts support using appropriately cautious language.
stimulus: A study found that children who participated in community service programs developed stronger senses of civic responsibility compared to children who did not participate. Additionally, these children later voted at higher rates as adults.
questionStem: Which one of the following inferences is most supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Community service is the only way to foster civic responsibility.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All children who participate in community service will become engaged citizens.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some children who participate in community service programs develop stronger civic responsibility.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Voting is more important than community service.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Civic responsibility causes people to vote.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that participants in service programs developed stronger senses of civic responsibility. At least some children had this outcome, making this modest claim strongly supported.
explanations.A: Too strong — the stimulus establishes a correlation, not exclusivity.
explanations.B: Too strong — while the group showed higher rates, not all will follow the pattern.
explanations.C: Correct — the data directly supports that at least some participants developed stronger responsibility.
explanations.D: Unsupported — the stimulus does not rank the importance of these outcomes.
explanations.E: Unsupported — the data shows a correlation but not causal direction.

difficultyReason: Technology observation with clear practical outcome. Correct answer is a simple, hedged inference that directly follows from the stated facts.
stimulus: A software company tested two versions of its application on groups of users. Version A included a simplified interface. Users of Version A reported spending less time learning the application and completed tasks more quickly than users of Version B.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: All software should use simplified interfaces.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Simplified interfaces make software universally better.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Some users experienced faster task completion with the simplified interface.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Version B is inherently flawed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Interface design is irrelevant to user experience.

explanations.correct: Users of Version A (simplified interface) completed tasks more quickly. This directly supports that at least some users experienced this advantage.
explanations.A: Too strong — the finding applies to this context, not universally to all software.
explanations.B: Too strong — simplification helped with speed and learning, but 'universally better' overstates this.
explanations.C: Correct — the data directly supports that some users completed tasks more quickly with Version A.
explanations.D: Unsupported — slower task completion does not make Version B inherently flawed.
explanations.E: Contradicted — the stimulus shows interface design does affect user performance.
